prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1394; do not mention it.)
text:
I am writing to advise that this office now represents the injured party in connection with the motor vehicle collision described above. Our client was injured in a low-speed head-on collision and is currently receiving medical care for those injuries. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to this office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person.

We request that you provide the bodily injury and property damage liability limits of the policy issued to your insured, together with a certified copy of the declarations page and any other policy documents that may apply to this loss. Please also confirm whether any other coverage, including umbrella or excess coverage, may be available.

We further ask that your company preserve all evidence relating to this collision. This includes the claim file, photographs, vehicle data and event data recorder information, repair estimates, recorded statements, adjuster notes, and any telematics or dash camera footage. Kindly confirm in writing within fourteen days that this preservation request has been received and that the evidence will be retained.
